deep.reconstruction:
Heading: 'Geometric side of ternary forms'. This page sets up the geometric interpretation of a positive ternary quadratic form as the metric (Gram) form of a lattice or affine frame in space.

(1) Frame. Fix an origin O. Let t, t', t'' be the 'transitions' (displacement vectors) from O to three points P, P', P'' that are not coplanar with O. When no confusion arises, the points themselves are written (t), (t'), (t'').

(2) Inner product. (t,t') is defined as |t|·|t'|·cos(angle between t and t'). In modern terms this is the scalar product t·t'. Gauss notes that it is bilinear: (Σ α_i t_i, Σ β_j u_j) is obtained by formally multiplying out (Σ α_i t_i)(Σ β_j u_j) and replacing each product t_i u_j by (t_i, u_j).

(3) Coordinates. Every point in space is represented by the trinomial x t + x' t' + x'' t''. These are affine, generally oblique, coordinates (x, x', x'').

(4) Planes. Every plane has an equation λx + λ'x' + λ''x'' = L. For the plane through the three points μt, μ't'', μ''t'' (intercepts μ, μ', μ'' on the three axes), substituting each point gives λμ = λ'μ' = λ''μ'' = L. This is the intercept form x/μ + x'/μ' + x''/μ'' = 1, up to the factor L. [The substitution step is mine; it is immediate.]

(5) The form and its adjoint. Set a = (t,t), a' = (t',t'), a'' = (t'',t''), b = (t',t''), b' = (t,t''), b'' = (t,t'). Then
|xt + x't' + x''t''|² = a x² + a' x'² + a'' x''² + 2b x'x'' + 2b' x x'' + 2b'' x x'.
So the ternary form (a, a', a''; b, b', b'') in Gauss's Disquisitiones notation is the Gram form of the frame.

The adjoint form is defined by
- A = a'a'' − b², A' = aa'' − b'², A'' = aa' − b''²,
- B = b'b'' − ab, B' = bb'' − a'b', B'' = bb' − a''b''.

The determinant is D = aa'a'' + 2bb'b'' − ab² − a'b'² − a''b''². These are exactly the cofactors (the adjugate) and the determinant of the Gram matrix G = [[a,b'',b'],[b'',a',b],[b',b,a'']]. D is the squared volume of the parallelepiped on t, t', t''.

The page serves as a preamble. The next page uses these quantities to build the reciprocal frame T = At + B''t' + B't'', etc. Each T is perpendicular to two of the t's, and T, T', T'' are D times the dual basis. The next page then derives the plane normal λT + λ'T' + λ''T'', the triangle area and tetrahedron volume, and the perpendicular distance.
errors: No mathematical errors found. All six adjoint coefficients and D agree with the cofactors and determinant of the Gram matrix [[a,b'',b'],[b'',a',b],[b',b,a'']].

Minor imprecision: the bilinearity statement is written schematically and the left-hand side is not completed ('Man hat allgemein (...,...)' is followed directly by 'wenn man ...'). The intended meaning is clear.

results.what: Representation of a ternary quadratic form as the squared-length (Gram) form of three non-coplanar vectors; coefficients are the scalar products
results.modern_name: Gram matrix / metric tensor of a lattice basis; geometric theory of positive ternary forms
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (review of Seeber, 1831; Nachlass piece printed in Werke II); later Dirichlet (1850)

results.what: Bilinearity of the scalar product (t,u) = |t||u|cos θ under formal multiplication
results.usually_credited_to: folklore; made systematic by Grassmann and Hamilton in the 1840s

results.what: Plane equation in oblique coordinates and intercept form λμ = λ'μ' = λ''μ'' = L
results.modern_name: intercept form of a plane in affine coordinates

results.what: Adjoint form (A, A', A''; B, B', B'') and determinant D of the ternary form
results.modern_name: adjugate matrix and determinant; adjoint ternary form

deep.surprise_reason: This is the standard setup for Gauss's geometric interpretation of ternary forms. That interpretation is known from his 1831 Seeber review, and this Nachlass text appears to be printed in Werke II (the pencil archival marks refer to it). The adjoint and determinant are straight from the Disquisitiones. Nothing on this page goes beyond what is already attributed to Gauss.

checkable.sympy: a,ap,app,b,bp,bpp=symbols('a ap app b bp bpp'); G=Matrix([[a,bpp,bp],[bpp,ap,b],[bp,b,app]]); simplify(G.det()-(a*ap*app+2*b*bp*bpp-a*b**2-ap*bp**2-app*bpp**2))
checkable.asserts: D as written equals the determinant of the Gram matrix (result 0)

checkable.sympy: A=ap*app-b**2; Ap=a*app-bp**2; App=a*ap-bpp**2; B=bp*bpp-a*b; Bp=b*bpp-ap*bp; Bpp=b*bp-app*bpp; Adj=Matrix([[A,Bpp,Bp],[Bpp,Ap,B],[Bp,B,App]]); simplify(Adj-G.adjugate())
checkable.asserts: A, A', A'', B, B', B'' are exactly the adjugate entries of G (zero matrix)
adj(G)·G = D·I; this underlies the next page's relations aT + b''T' + b'T'' = Dt, etc. (zero matrix)

checkable.sympy: t=Matrix(symbols('t1:4')); u=Matrix(symbols('u1:4')); w=Matrix(symbols('w1:4')); x,y,z=symbols('x y z'); v=x*t+y*u+z*w; expand(v.dot(v)-(x**2*t.dot(t)+y**2*u.dot(u)+z**2*w.dot(w)+2*y*z*u.dot(w)+2*x*z*t.dot(w)+2*x*y*t.dot(u)))
checkable.asserts: Squared length of x t + x' t' + x'' t'' is the ternary form with a = (t,t), b = (t',t''), etc. (result 0)

checkable.sympy: mu,mup,mupp,L=symbols('mu mup mupp L'); lam,lamp,lampp=L/mu,L/mup,L/mupp; [simplify(lam*mu-L), simplify(lamp*mup-L), simplify(lampp*mupp-L)]
checkable.asserts: The plane λx + λ'x' + λ''x'' = L passes through (μ,0,0), (0,μ',0), (0,0,μ'') iff λμ = λ'μ' = λ''μ'' = L

checkable.sympy: T=A*t+Bpp*u+Bp*w with t.dot(t)=a, u.dot(u)=ap, w.dot(w)=app, u.dot(w)=b, t.dot(w)=bp, t.dot(u)=bpp => simplify(A*bpp+Bpp*ap+Bp*b) == 0 and simplify(A*bp+Bpp*b+Bp*app) == 0
checkable.asserts: T = At + B''t' + B't'' is orthogonal to t' and t'' (the next page's claim), as a consequence of these definitions

transcription_corrections: The definition line reads 'das Product der Länge der beiden Linien t, t' in den Cosinus ihrer Neigung', with an interlinear insertion above 'Länge' (possibly 'kürzesten Entfern...'). The base text says lengths, which is what the scalar-product definition requires.

The left-hand side of the bilinearity formula reads (αt + α't' + α''t'' + ..., βu + β'u' + β''u'' + ...). The second set of coefficients is written as Gothic/script b (𝔟), as transcribed, and the first coefficient's prime marks are partly smudged.
The pencil archival marks at the top left read roughly 'S. 30[3]' and 'II S. 348', likely references to a printed edition.
